section: 2. **Decompose** — Split any task with more than 2–3 steps into a phase chain, one task per phase. Never emit compound instructions.

fixtures.application: I need something runnable on my local 7B model (reasoning off, 8k context). The job: take the chat transcript I paste, pull out every question the customer asked, group those questions by topic, then draft one FAQ entry per topic using the best question phrasing, each entry as `FAQ-ENTRY: <question> / <answer>`. From experience this model fumbles any instruction that asks it to do two things, and I need to run each step separately and feed its output forward by hand. I can't answer follow-ups here — assume whatever you still need, note each assumption in a line, and give me the complete set of prompts in one go.

variants.v1: 2. **Decompose** — More than 2–3 steps means the file holds one `## Phase` section per step, and each phase's prompt asks for exactly one thing; a prompt that asks for two steps is a bug — split it, never reword it.
variants.v2: 2. **Decompose** — Count the steps the task needs. More than 2–3 means the deliverable is a chain of single-task phases whose outputs feed forward; never deliver the steps as one compound instruction.
variants.v3: 2. **Decompose** — one step per phase, always. Four steps in the task means four `## Phase` sections; a phase may name only one action.

section: 4. **Draft the exemplars** — For each phase that needs few-shot demonstration, draft 1–3 input/output pairs. Give reasoning phases worked chains-of-thought, not bare answers. Present the exemplars inside the Spec block.

fixtures.application: Design a prompt for my local 3B model (reasoning off, 4k context). I paste a batch of support tickets and it counts how many tickets mention each of three product areas — Flibber, Gasket, or Hinge — reporting the counts as `Flibber: n` style lines. Brutal experience with this model: it only does what a shown example does, verbatim in structure — an example that shows a bare answer makes it guess; an example that counts out loud makes it count. The demonstration pairs are the part I'll check most carefully before anything goes in the file. I can't do back-and-forth — assume the rest, note assumptions in a line, and give me the complete prompt file including the demonstration pairs in one go.

variants.v1: 4. **Draft the exemplars** — Each phase that needs demonstration gets 1–3 input/output pairs, shown in the Spec block for sign-off. For counting, ranking, or logic phases, each pair's output walks through the work step by step before landing on the answer; an output that jumps straight to the answer is a bare-answer exemplar — redo it.
variants.v2: 4. **Draft the exemplars** — Demonstration pairs live in the Spec block's `Exemplars:` field, 1–3 per demonstrated phase. A reasoning phase's pairs must each show a worked chain in the output (one visible step per line, ending in the answer); `input → bare answer` pairs teach the model to skip the reasoning.
variants.v3: 4. **Draft the exemplars** — 1–3 input/output pairs per demonstrated phase, presented inside the Spec block; a reasoning pair is only valid when its output shows the intermediate work.

section: - **Always end with a format contract** — labeled slots (`Answer: ___`) and a stop condition; small models drift from schemas.

fixtures.application: Design a prompt for my local 4B model (reasoning off, 6k context). I feed it one product review and it must answer exactly three things: overall sentiment (positive or negative), the single biggest complaint if there is one, and a one-word topic. I've learned this model rambles unless the end of the prompt shows it precisely where to type — it performs when there's a labeled blank sitting there waiting. I need the answer as `SENTIMENT: ...`, `COMPLAINT: ...`, `TOPIC: ...` lines and nothing after the topic line. I can't answer follow-ups — assume whatever you need, note it in a line, and give me the complete prompt in one go.

markers.stop-sentence: (?i)\b(stop( here| after the last line)?|nothing else|end of (the )?output|no (further|other|extra|additional) text|that'?s (it|all))\b

variants.v1: - **Always end with a format contract** — the last lines of every phase prompt are the labeled empty slots the model fills (`Answer: ___`, one slot per expected answer line) followed by one sentence telling the model to stop after the last slot. A phase that trails off in an open-ended instruction will drift.
variants.v2: - **Always end with a format contract** — every phase prompt closes with its labeled blanks (`SENTIMENT: ___` style, one per answer line) and a single stop sentence; a prose description of the format is not a contract.
variants.v3: - Close each phase with labeled slots (`Answer: ___`) plus one stop sentence; prose format descriptions alone let the model drift.

section: - **Front-load every prompt** — task statement first, minimal context; shared material lives once in the file's Shared context section.

fixtures.application: Design prompts for my local 5B model (reasoning off, 8k context, and the budget is tight because other prompts share the session). We grade customer feedback on our own scale: 'sev-red' means the customer cannot complete the task at all, 'sev-amber' means they can work around it, 'sev-green' is cosmetic. The job has two parts: first grade each feedback item in a pasted batch, then tally counts per severity for the weekly report. Both parts need the scale. The graded items must come out as `ITEM <id> -> sev-red` style lines. I can't do back-and-forth — assume whatever is unclear, note it in a line, and give me the complete set of prompts in one go.

variants.v1: - **Front-load every prompt** — each phase prompt opens with its task sentence; anything two or more phases need (definitions, scales, formats) is written once in the file's `## Shared context` section and referred to by name — never restated inside a phase.
variants.v2: - **Front-load every prompt** — the file states its target first, then `## Shared context` carries every shared definition exactly once; each phase prompt starts with its one task sentence and references shared material by name. Never open a phase with context.
variants.v3: - Phase prompts start with the task, never with context. Material needed by two or more phases lives one time in `## Shared context`.

section: - **Add a self-consistency harness note** when a phase is high-stakes reasoning — `<!-- harness: run 3 samples, majority-vote -->` in the phase header.

section: - **Require mechanical verification** — the Verification method is a check a harness can run (regex, parse, diff, test); small models self-critique poorly.

fixtures.application: Design a prompt for my local 4B model (reasoning off, 6k context): it reads a pasted config file and lists every key whose value is not one of the allowed tokens ON, OFF, or AUTO. variants.v1: - **Require mechanical verification** — the file ends with a `## Verification` section whose checks a script can execute (regex over output lines, diff against a fixture, parse and count). 'Review the output' or a live model run is not a verification method.
variants.v2: - **Require mechanical verification** — the Verification method is a check a harness can run (regex, parse, diff, test); small models self-critique poorly. Write the check commands, not review instructions.
variants.v3: - Every file's last section is `## Verification` with runnable checks — regex, diff, or parse plus count. Subjective review is not verification.

## Prompt File Template

```markdown
# Prompt chain: <task title>

Target: <model>, reasoning <on|off>, <context budget> context.

## Run instructions (for the executing agent)

<facts and definitions every phase needs, written once>

## Phase N — <name>

Input: <what this phase receives, from where>
Output: <the format the next phase or the user expects>
```

section: - Never repeat Shared context inside a phase — duplication burns the context window and drifts when edited in one place.

fixtures.application: Design prompts for my local 4B model (reasoning off, 12k context). We process warranty claims in three passes: pass one decides whether the claim qualifies, pass two computes the refund from our price table, pass three writes the customer reply. All three passes need the price table — Zorblax Basic 50, Zorblax Pro 120, Zorblax Max 200 — and the refund rules (refund = table price × 0.8 for qualifying claims, 0 otherwise). The passes run one after another in a single session, output feeding forward. This model gets visibly worse when the same paragraph is repeated to it across prompts, so I need each pass's prompt kept lean. I can't do back-and-forth — assume whatever is unclear, note it in a line, and give me the complete set of prompts in one go.

variants.v1: - Never repeat Shared context inside a phase — phases refer to shared material by name ('using the price table above'); duplication burns the context window and drifts when edited in one place.
variants.v2: - Shared definitions and tables are written exactly once, in `## Shared context`. A phase that re-states shared material instead of referencing it is a bug, even when the phase would read better self-contained.
variants.v3: - One copy of shared material, in `## Shared context`; phases reference it by name. Never inline it.

section: - Keep run instructions to a sentence or two — the small model executes them too, and preamble conditionals are the compound instructions this skill exists to avoid. Phase inputs stay in context in a single-session run; never add paste placeholders.

fixtures.application: Design a prompt for my local 4B model (reasoning off, 8k context). It takes a pasted job description and extracts required skills as `SKILL: ...` lines. I run it by hand — I paste the JD into the same chat and it answers. One wrinkle: half the time I forget to paste the JD until after I've already sent the prompt, so whatever you write needs to cope with that gracefully. I can't answer follow-ups — assume whatever you need, note it in a line, and give me the complete prompt in one go.

variants.v1: - Keep run instructions to a sentence or two — the small model executes them too: 'Run each phase in order; the inputs are already in this conversation.' No if-branches and no paste placeholders — preamble conditionals are compound instructions, and placeholders invite the model to echo them.
variants.v2: - `## Run instructions` is one or two sentences total; the executing model reads them as task instructions, so conditional preambles and `[PASTE ...]`-style placeholders are bugs, not helpful scaffolding.
variants.v3: - Run instructions: a sentence or two, no conditionals, no paste placeholders. Inputs are already in the conversation.
